transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-17   Start: 15:00 PDT   Duration: 44 mins
Attendees: Maya (Redwood CSM), Derek (Redwood SE), Jordan (LynxWare CTO), Anya (Platform Lead), Samir (Security)

Summary:
Quick activation kickoff to align on networking, security controls, capacity, and a 4-week pilot runway. Focus on VPC/private deployment options, KMS integration, and go/no-go criteria. Agreed next steps and owners at end.

Topics: onboarding runbook, VPC peering, dedicated vs hosted, SSO/SAML, KMS/encryption, pilot metrics, rollback plan

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: All right good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, I'm the CSM for LynxWare. Quick roll call before we jump in?
[00:06] Jordan: Jordan here, CTO at LynxWare. Hey all.
[00:08] Anya: Anya, Platform.
[00:10] Samir: Samir, Security.
[00:12] Derek: Derek from Redwood, SE, I'll cover the infra bits.
[00:16] Maya: Great. Objective today is a practical walkthrough of the activation runbook and to capture any constraints for VPC/on-prem, KMS, and timeline. We'll surface any blockers for the pilot.
[00:26] Jordan: Sounds good. We want to validate latency for our internal search use case and make sure we can keep PII inside our VPC.
[00:33] Samir: Yeah and to echo that, compliance and audit logs are must-haves — SOC2-ish controls, plus we need to understand retention and how logs flow back to our SIEM.
[00:43] Derek: Okay great, we'll run through the networking steps first. For Private mode we support both VPC peering and PrivateLink style setups, usually customers pick peering for lower ops. There can be some NAT config for egress.
[00:55] Anya: Quick question — we've got strict egress rules, can you support a fully private deployment with no public egress to the inference hosts?
[01:02] Derek: Yes, we can. There are two options: private control plane with a customer-managed VPC where inference nodes sit in your subnet and Redwood's control plane communicates over a secured management channel; or an on-prem package if you want air-gapped. Both can be configured to limit egress. There may be small exceptions for image updates unless you use the on-prem bundle.
[01:24] Jordan: When would you recommend dedicated vs hosted for us? We're starting small but expect spikes in peak traffic during batch inference jobs.
[01:32] Maya: Typically for a security-conscious company with predictable peak windows, Dedicated is recommended because you get reserved capacity, more predictable latency, and isolation. Hosted is faster to get started and cheaper at low volume.
[01:42] Derek: I'll add — Dedicated gives you autoscaling policies, but if your bursts are unpredictable we can configure burst capacity. Also, we can size GPUs based on seq lengths and token rates. If you share a sample traffic profile we'll give a cost/throughput tradeoff.
[01:58] Anya: We'll pull that today — is there a specific histogram format you want?
[02:01] Derek: A simple CSV with columns [timestamp, request_count, avg_seq_len, 95th_seq_len] for a week is perfect.
[02:09] Samir: On KMS — we need to use our Vault HSM. Do you support customer-managed KMS and bring-your-own keys?
[02:16] Derek: Yes, BYOK is supported for Private and Dedicated. For Hosted we also support envelope encryption with customer KMS in some regions. We'll need your KMS metadata and access policies so we can set up the integration.
[02:27] Jordan: Are audit logs delivered to Splunk or S3? Our security team wants immutable logs in S3 with lifecycle rules.
[02:33] Maya: We can export audit logs to S3 or a syslog endpoint; S3 delivery is common and we support server-side encryption. We can also push to your Splunk via forwarder if you prefer.
[02:42] Samir: How long are logs retained by Redwood? We may want a short window on Redwood side but ship everything to our archive.
[02:48] Derek: By default we retain 30 days, but retention is configurable with enterprise plans. Many customers mirror to their S3 and set long-term retention there.
[02:55] Jordan: Ok good. Let's talk about SSO — we'll use SAML, we have strict SCIM provisioning too.
[03:00] Maya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Derek, do we have any special notes?
[03:05] Derek: Make sure the SAML assertion includes team or group attribute if you want RBAC mapping. We map Red- roles to Redwood roles by group claim. Also for SCIM we recommend starting with manual invite for the pilot then enabling full provisioning after staging.
[03:18] Anya: Noted. A couple of nitty-gritty things — we use a lot of KV cache in our inference layer, how do you handle KV cache persistence across node restarts?
[03:27] Derek: We maintain KV cache in shared memory per GPU instance and we support warm-starting caches via a snapshot mechanism. There might be some cache warm-up on failover but we do best-effort to preserve context.
[03:38] Jordan: Did you say K V cash in the transcript? (laughter)
[03:41] Maya: (laughs) transcript gods.
[03:44] Derek: On performance benchmarks — if you want we can run a short internal perf test against a synthetic workload that mirrors your profile. That usually takes 48–72 hours to schedule.
[03:54] Jordan: We'd appreciate that. We'll prioritize the sample histogram and a small corpus.
[03:59] Samir: Another compliance question: do you have a documented key rotation process and proof for cert auditors?
[04:05] Derek: Yes we have a key rotation policy and can provide SOC2-ready docs. For BYOK we show the integration steps and rotation is done on your KMS side; we accept rotated key IDs as long as you make them available.
[04:16] Anya: In terms of observability — what do we get out of the box? Token-level cost, latency percentiles, per-model dashboards?
[04:23] Maya: Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdowns, per-route and per-model latency p95/p99, error traces, and you can hook tracing to your APM. We also have alerting for regression on eval sets.
[04:35] Derek: We can set up a dashboard for your pilot routes and give you a shared view. We'll also instrument request IDs so you can correlate logs.
[04:43] Jordan: For the pilot success criteria — let's codify it: p95 latency under 200ms for synchronous search queries, throughput of 100 qps sustained for 10 minutes, and data residency inside our VPC. Does that sound reasonable?
[04:56] Maya: That's a good start. We'll add error rate under 0.5% and completeness — meaning output quality compared to your benchmark prompts — to the list.
[05:04] Anya: About the pilot timeline — do you have a recommended sequence?
[05:07] Maya: Week 0: provisioning and networking. Week 1: baseline perf and smoke tests. Week 2–3: pilot traffic with shadowing and controlled rollout. Week 4: production cutover decision.
[05:18] Jordan: We can commit to that, but need the runbook to share with infra.
[05:22] Maya: I'll send the runbook draft after this meeting. It contains the exact security checklist, SAML metadata fields, VPC config snippets, and validation commands.
[05:30] Samir: Legal wanted to check data retention on embeddings and prompting logs — are these persisted by Redwood?
[05:36] Derek: We can disable non-essential retention for Hosted, and in Private/Dedicated you control retention and where artifacts are stored. For embeddings, you can elect to keep or delete after inference; we'll provide API flags.
[05:46] Anya: Good to hear. A practical question: who is our daily contact during the pilot?
[05:50] Maya: I'll be primary CSM. Derek will be the escalation SE. If you need account-level changes we have a Customer Success patch process — contact list in the runbook.
[05:59] Jordan: OK. Anything we missed?
[06:02] (brief silence)
[06:05] Maya: Let's recap next steps. I'll share runbook & dashboard links (due Thu 20th). Anya to export traffic profile; Samir to confirm KMS provider and compliance docs; Derek to produce dedicated capacity sizing and cost estimate. Schedule the sizing call for week of 24th.
[06:22] Jordan: One more — is there a recommended staging config for model variants? We often test a smaller quantized variant first.
[06:29] Derek: Yes, you can pin model versions and we support rollouts and automatic fallback to a quantized variant on capacity constraints. We'll document the rollout policy steps in the runbook.
[06:40] Anya: Great. Any blockers from security?
[06:43] Samir: Nothing blocker-level, just need the SOC2 package and KMS integration doc for legal review. If those look good we can get network approvals.
[06:52] Maya: Got it. Action items captured. I'll also include a sample playbook for incident escalation and rollback which several customers found helpful.
[07:02] Jordan: Perfect. If we get the runbook today we can prep the VPC peering request and come back to you with details.
[07:08] Maya: Awesome. We'll send the links after the call. Anything else before we wrap?
[07:12] Derek: I just flagged the perf test — we'll need a time window and a test token; I'll coordinate that in separate email.
[07:18] Jordan: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:20] Maya: Thanks all, ending now.
[07:23] (meeting ends)

Meeting length ~44 minutes.

Notes on transcript quality: speaker labels are mostly correct but a few short crosstalks were merged; some technical terms (KV cache) may be transcribed with minor errors.

Final recap (as calendar note):
- Pilot window: ~4 weeks starting on provisioning
- Success criteria: p95 <200ms, throughput 100 qps sustained, error rate <0.5%, data in VPC
- Delivery: Runbook + dashboard (Maya), traffic profile (Anya), KMS/compliance docs (Samir), capacity estimate (Derek)

End of file.
